humanities_role_explanation: Designed to evaluate graduate-level and expert-level historical knowledge and comprehension, explicitly targeting disciplinary competence in global history.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Textual questions and answers presented in a four-option multiple-choice format.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Testing factual recall of expert-level global history, specifically societal structures and temporal-regional facts, through a four-choice multiple-choice QA format.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Specifically scoped to the domain of global history rather than general-purpose multi-task evaluation.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates seven models from the Gemini, OpenAI (GPT-4-Turbo), and Llama (Llama-3.1-8B) families.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates model performance using balanced accuracy.

summary: This paper introduces the History Seshat Test for LLMs (HiST-LLM), a benchmark derived from the Seshat Global History Databank to evaluate models on expert graduate-level historical knowledge. Spanning 36,000 data points across 600 historical societies, the benchmark reveals that current LLMs outperform random guessing but still fall significantly short of human expert comprehension.
key_findings: The evaluated LLMs achieved balanced accuracies ranging from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46.0% (GPT-4-Turbo), outperforming the 25% random baseline. Models demonstrated better performance on earlier historical periods and exhibited regional imbalances, performing best on the Americas and worst on Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa.
review_notes: Cip's benchmark name was used as it includes the full expansion provided in the text. No other significant disagreements.
facets_explanation: The HiST-LLM benchmark is constructed from a subset of the Seshat Global History Databank, a pre-existing structured database of historical data reviewed and assembled by history experts and graduate research assistants. Answering the questions requires domain-specific historical knowledge not present in the prompt stimulus. The evaluation uses a four-choice multiple-choice format, and the treatment of annotator disagreement is not addressed in the provided text.
results_explanation: The paper reports that 'GPT-4-Turbo' achieved the best performance with a balanced accuracy of '46%' ('ranging from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46% (GPT-4-Turbo)') on a 'four-choice format' benchmark. The format gap and human gap fields are null because the paper evaluates a single multiple-choice format and reports no quantified human baseline, only noting that models fall 'short of expert comprehension'. Regional asymmetry is explicitly identified as a finding, with performance being 'better for the Americas and lowest in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa for the more advanced models'.
